answer: A single kernel checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called a whisper, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so a hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. Forging 105 aliases therefore burns 177 bonds held for 13 days each, plus the karst attestations those aliases can never earn. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
